title: Tensoring an extension by zero
statement:
Let $j:U\hookrightarrow Y$ be an
open immersion, and use
the finite coefficient ring
$A$. For $K\in D(U,A)$ and $M\in D(Y,A)$, there is a natural
isomorphism

$$
(j_!K)\otimes_A^LM\simeq j_!(K\otimes_A^Lj^*M),
$$

where $j_!$ is extension by
zero, tensor is the derived
tensor product, and $j^*$ is the
derived pullback.

proof.text: Work throughout with modules over the constant ring sheaves on the small pro-etale sites, in the small site models of def-weil-pbc-proetale-site. By lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization, identify $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}/U$ and $A_U$ with $A_Y|_U$. The comparison lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-comparison identifies the actual module inverse image with slice restriction, so this is the $j^*$ in the assertion. The presheaf defining def-weil-extension-by-zero agrees with the slice extension presheaf: an object has at most one map to the open $U$, hence its indexing direct sum is either the specified value or zero. Thus lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact applies to these very functors: $j_!\dashv j^*$ and both are exact. Exactness identifies $H^n(j_!C)$ with $j_!H^n(C)$ and $H^n(j^*D)$ with $j^*H^n(D)$, since kernels and images in $\ker d^n/\operatorname{im}d^{n-1}$ are preserved. In particular acyclic complexes and quasi-isomorphisms are preserved. By lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated these degreewise functors induce functors on the unbounded derived categories. The finite-level definition def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom identifies derived pullback with this exact degreewise $j^*$.

proof.text: Apply lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-extension-tensor with $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)=(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_Y)$ and its object $U$. For every sheaf $P$ on $U$ and $N$ on $Y$, its inverse gives a sheaf isomorphism $\theta_{P,N}:(j_!P)\otimes_A N\xrightarrow{\sim}j_!(P\otimes_Aj^*N)$ natural simultaneously in $P,N$. The ring restriction and extension functors are precisely those identified in step 1, so no comparison between etale and pro-etale coefficient categories is involved.

Because $j_!$ is a left adjoint, lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits makes it commute with the small coproduct indexed by $\{(p,q)\in\mathbf Z^2:p+q=n\}$, for each integer $n$. Apply $\theta_{P^p,N^q}$ to every summand of the tensor complex of def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves and then this coproduct isomorphism. This gives, for arbitrary unbounded complexes, $\Theta_{P,N}:\operatorname{Tot}(j_!P\otimes_A N)\xrightarrow{\sim}j_!\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_Aj^*N)$. Naturality of $\theta$ with respect to $d_P^p$ and $d_N^q$ identifies the two summand differentials $d_P^p\otimes1$ and $1\otimes d_N^q$; additivity of $j_!$ also preserves the factor $(-1)^p$. The maps therefore commute with the total differential $d_P\otimes1+(-1)^p1\otimes d_N$, and their termwise inverses do too. The same summand naturality proves that $\Theta$ commutes with every pair of chain maps.

proof.text: Extension by zero preserves K-flat complexes. Indeed, if $P$ is K-flat on $U$ and $N$ acyclic on $Y$, exactness makes $j^*N$ acyclic; hence $\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_Aj^*N)$ is acyclic by def-pc-kflat-complex (using the symmetry of the tensor complex), and exactness of $j_!$ and step 3 show $\operatorname{Tot}(j_!P\otimes_A N)$ is acyclic. The symmetry here is the summand exchange $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{pq}y\otimes x$ for degrees $p,q$; it commutes with the displayed total differentials. The underlying sheaf symmetry is part of lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed. Moreover $j_!$ preserves flat sheaves: for a flat sheaf $F$ on $U$, step 2 identifies $j_!F\otimes_A-$ with $j_!\circ(F\otimes_A-)\circ j^*$; each factor is exact, so their composite is exact. The sheaf symmetry in lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed identifies this functor with $-\otimes_Aj_!F$, which is the tensor order in def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules. Consequently a K-flat complex with flat terms remains such after $j_!$.

proof.text: Choose representatives of $K$ and $M$ and K-flat resolutions $P\to K$ and $Q\to M$ with flat terms using lem-pc-kflat-resolution on the two ringed sites. By step 1, $j_!P$ represents $j_!K$ and $j^*Q$ represents $j^*M$; by step 4 the first is K-flat with flat terms. The construction def-weil-proetale-inverse-image supplies the actual morphism of pro-etale sites for the scheme morphism $j$, hence a morphism of topoi, with its specified constant-ring structure map. Step 1 identifies its module pullback with restriction to the localized ringed site of def-pur-localized-ringed-site and identifies its inverse-image ring with $A_U$. Apply lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat to this morphism, with ring map $j^{-1}A_Y\cong A_U$: it shows that $j^*Q$ is also K-flat with flat terms. The computation isomorphisms of lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent, for the derived tensor of def-weil-derived-tensor, now identify the two sides of $\Theta_{P,Q}$ in step 3 with $(j_!K)\otimes_A^LM$ and $j_!(K\otimes_A^Lj^*M)$ respectively. Localizing $\Theta_{P,Q}$ gives the required isomorphism.

proof.text: The isomorphism is natural in derived objects, not just in chosen complexes. Apply the equivalence $W_R^{-1}\mathcal P_R\simeq D(R)$ in lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent separately to $R=A_U$ and $R=A_Y$. Here $\mathcal P_R$ consists of K-flat complexes with flat terms in the homotopy category. The construction $\Theta$ of step 3 respects homotopies explicitly: if $f-g=d h+h d$ in the first variable, use $h\otimes1$ on each total summand; if $f-g=d t+t d$ in the second variable, use $(-1)^p1\otimes t$ on the summand of first degree $p$. In each case $dH+Hd$ is the difference of the induced tensor maps. Summand naturality of $\theta$ for $h$ or $t$, and additivity of $j_!$, identify these homotopies on both sides of $\Theta$. It is therefore natural on $\mathcal P_{A_U}\times\mathcal P_{A_Y}$. On quasi-isomorphisms both sides become invertible after localization, by the exact functors of step 1 and the tensor computation isomorphisms of lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent. A naturality square for an invertible map also commutes for its inverse, by composing the square with those inverses. Every morphism of the two localizations is a composite of maps and inverted quasi-isomorphisms. Hence these squares extend to all pairs of localized morphisms, proving simultaneous naturality in $K,M$ and independence of the resolutions under their canonical derived identifications. The inverse family descends in the same way, so this is a natural isomorphism.
